name: Isolated serial interface (UART/SPI/I2C)
description: Digital isolators with an isolated supply for UART/SPI/I2C across a safety or ground-loop barrier.
electrical_characteristics: Digital isolator channel count and direction
Isolated DC-DC or transformer driver for the far side
critical_electrical_constraints: Barrier creepage per the declared isolation voltage; isolator package creepage >= requirement
No copper under the isolator barrier
Isolated supply decoupled on both sides
stackup_recommendations: 2 layers for low-speed buses; 4 layers when USB or Ethernet differential pairs are present
placement_rules: Transceiver as close to its connector as the protection parts allow; protection between connector and transceiver
Termination resistors at the bus end; bias resistors at the transceiver
Isolated interfaces: isolator straddles the barrier, isolated supply next to it
routing_rules: Differential pairs (USB 90 ohm, Ethernet 100 ohm, CAN/RS-485 120 ohm) per the standard; matched lengths
Shield/chassis ground ring at the connector, joined to logic ground at one point or via a capacitor per the product grounding plan
Short stubs on multidrop buses; no vias in the differential pair where avoidable
copper_ground_requirements: Ground plane under transceivers; keep-out under the isolation barrier
thermal_considerations: Bus-powered boards: regulator dissipation at the maximum port voltage
emi_emc_considerations: Common-mode chokes on USB/Ethernet where the product is EMC tested; ferrite on shield ground
protection_requirements: TVS on every bus line rated for the bus voltage and the surge/ESD level required
Fuse or current limiter on supplied power (VBUS, PoE, bus power)
verification_requirements: Differential pair geometry recorded against the fabricator stackup
Termination and bias values from the transceiver datasheet
Interface compliance (eye diagram, bit-error) is a hardware test
manufacturing_constraints: Connector footprints from the manufacturer drawing; through-hole connectors for mechanical strain
